BiblicalUsage: The lion in Daniel is the Aramaic lion, and it is the beast of the den and the beast of the vision. Daniel is cast into the den of lions, and in the morning he tells the king that his God has sent His angel and shut the lions' mouths; and in the later vision the first beast is like a lion, with eagle's wings, standing as a man.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Daniel's lions are the proof that God rules the beasts men use to kill His people: the mouths are shut, the man comes out alive, and the empire that fed men to lions is itself the lion in the vision, a beast with wings that will lose them. And I hold that the God who shuts lions' mouths still does, for the people who will not bow.
